idea-plugin.name: Jupyter Notebook
idea-plugin.description:
Open, edit, and run Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) directly inside your IDE. The plugin launches an IPython kernel on your project's own Python interpreter and talks to it over ZeroMQ — no external Jupyter server required.

Features

  • Native notebook editor — code and Markdown cells with add / delete / reorder, rendered output (text, HTML, images, error tracebacks).
  • Python syntax highlighting with cross-cell awareness — variables, functions and imports defined in earlier cells are highlighted in later ones.
  • Inline diagnostics — syntax errors, undefined names (not defined in this or an earlier cell) and unresolved imports are underlined, with an IDE-style tooltip describing the problem. Uses pyflakes when available and falls back to a built-in analyzer otherwise.
  • Go to definition — Cmd/Ctrl+Click or Cmd/Ctrl+B on a variable jumps to where it was defined and highlights its other uses; hovering with the modifier shows a clickable link.
  • Editor shortcuts inside cells — comment line (Cmd+/), duplicate line (Cmd+D), delete line (Cmd+⌫), move line (Opt+Shift+↑/↓).
  • Find & Replace — Cmd/Ctrl+F searches across cell sources, rendered Markdown and outputs with highlighted matches and a match counter; Cmd/Ctrl+R adds replace and replace-all for code cells.
  • Run & advance — Shift+Enter runs a cell and, once it finishes successfully, moves focus to the next cell, creating a new one if it was the last.
  • IDE-global shortcuts pass through — Search Everywhere, Find in Files, Go to File and Recent Files keep working while the notebook is focused.
  • Kernel management — automatic interpreter detection, on-demand kernel start, restart, interrupt, and auto-install of ipykernel; the working directory is the notebook's folder.
  • Standard format — reads and writes nbformat v4, fully compatible with JupyterLab and VS Code. Saves with Cmd+S.

Requires a Python 3.8+ interpreter with ipykernel (offered automatically on first run).

Source code on GitHub. Issues and pull requests are welcome — and if the plugin saves you some time, a ⭐ on the repo helps others find it.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.2.2

  • Fix: a notebook could fail to open with a blank/dead tab if the IDE hit a transient error reading the plugin's bundled resources (a memory-mapped ZipException). The editor now retries the read, caches resources once loaded, and — if it still can't read them — shows a clear "restart the IDE" message instead of failing silently. Inline analysis recovers from the same glitch instead of switching off.

0.2.1

  • Find & Replace: Cmd/Ctrl+F opens an in-notebook find bar that searches code, rendered Markdown and outputs, highlights every match and shows a match count; Enter / Shift+Enter jump between matches.
  • Replace: Cmd/Ctrl+R adds a replace row with Replace and Replace All for code cells.
  • Fix: Cmd/Ctrl+R no longer reloads and blanks the notebook view; correct match offsets for non-ASCII text; Cmd+S and global navigation shortcuts keep working while the find bar is focused.

0.2.0

  • Inline diagnostics: syntax errors, undefined variables and unresolved imports are now underlined, with hover tooltips explaining each problem.
  • Go to definition & usages: Cmd/Ctrl+Click or Cmd/Ctrl+B on a variable navigates to its definition and highlights its other uses; modifier-hover shows a link affordance.
  • In-cell editor shortcuts: comment (Cmd+/), duplicate (Cmd+D), delete and move line.
  • IDE-global shortcuts (Search Everywhere, Find in Files, Go to File, Recent Files) now work while the notebook is focused.
  • Shift+Enter runs a cell and advances to the next on success, creating a new cell after the last one.
  • File-type icon for .ipynb files in the project view.
  • Fixes: Markdown cells containing line breaks or special characters now render correctly; more reliable Shift+Enter handling; correct caret/column behavior with non-ASCII text.

0.1.0

  • Initial release: open, view, edit and execute .ipynb notebooks using the project's Python environment.
  • Code and Markdown cells, Python syntax highlighting, rich output rendering, and full kernel lifecycle management over ZeroMQ.
